Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-1-prompt-long-0081", "row_sha256": "01a27d165b82172eebbe9f4e9b01a44f983c4c2afbb270eb4d5a9837bb8999c4", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "
could you turn these notes into a clear request for a short correction for the Northbank Record? it should be a standalone local newspaper correction, not a new event preview. the correction concerns a community supper mentioned in the paper’s May 8 issue, in the item called “A supper at St. Luke’s.” Readers who saw that item need the right date, time and venue, and the notice should make clear who is organizing the supper. Keep the request focused on correcting what the paper got wrong; we don’t need a retelling of the original article or a general piece about neighborhood meals.

there are a few details that have been getting tangled together in my notes. the published item said the supper would be at St. Luke’s Church on June 15, with the meal starting at 6:00 p.m. Both of those details were wrong. It is at Riverside Fellowship Hall, 22 Alder Street, with the entrance on Juniper Lane. The date is June 14; doors open at 5:15 p.m. and the meal begins at 5:30 p.m. Please distinguish the door-opening time from the meal time rather than collapsing them into one. The event is free and open to the neighborhood, and people do not need a reservation. Those access details are still correct, so there is no need to present them as corrections.

The organizer’s name also needs to be handled accurately. East Ward Table is a volunteer group, and it is organizing the supper. It is independent of St. Luke’s Church; the event is not a church program. The wrong venue in the May 8 item may have left readers thinking the church was hosting it, so the correction should identify East Ward Table without suggesting that the group is part of the church. Don’t imply that the church arranged the event, endorsed it, or will be serving as the venue. There is no need to assign fault for the original mistake or explain how it happened.

A volunteer coordinator gave us this sentence: “We want neighbors to have the right door and the right evening.” Please use that sentence as an ordinary quote from the East Ward Table volunteer coordinator, if it fits naturally in a short correction. Keep the wording exactly as supplied and don’t turn it into a statement from the newspaper. The coordinator did not give us a name to attach, so identify the speaker only by that role. The quote is about helping neighbors find the supper, not about the history of the group or the cause of the error.

For the factual parts, it may help to keep the correction organized around these points rather than follow the mistaken item’s order:
1. Name the May 8 item, “A supper at St. Luke’s,” as the item being corrected.
2. State that the supper is organized by East Ward Table, an independent volunteer group, not by St. Luke’s Church.
3. Give the corrected venue and entrance, then the date and the separate door and meal times.
4. Retain the accurate information that the supper is free, open to the neighborhood and requires no reservation.

Please draft a short correction of around 130 to 170 words. A possible heading is “Correction: East Ward Table supper details.” Use plain newspaper language and make it easy for someone scanning the paper to notice the corrected date and address. It should be factual and calm, not an apology essay, event advertisement or invitation written in the group’s voice. We need to acknowledge that the May 8 item misstated the location and date and gave the wrong meal time, while giving the accurate details in their place. Don’t invent an explanation for the errors or suggest that the schedule has changed since publication. The times above are the correct schedule.

The correction can appear as text in the print edition and on the newspaper’s website; do not publish photos with it. There is no supplied photograph to choose from, and the request is not for a photo caption or a redesigned event listing. A reader should be able to understand the correction from the text alone. Keep the quotation in ordinary reported speech if you include it, and don’t add an unprovided name, phone number, email address, reservation method or other way to contact the organizers.

The paper’s issue is the Northbank Record’s regular local edition, and this is a correction about an item that appeared there on May 8. It should read as the newspaper setting the record straight, without implying that the corrected notice has already run or that anyone has approved a final version. Please keep the distinction between the erroneous information and the correct information unmistakable, especially the June 14 date, the 5:15 p.m. door opening and the 5:30 p.m. meal. The supper is at Riverside Fellowship Hall, 22 Alder Street, entered from Juniper Lane, not at the church. The final wording should leave readers with the correct practical details and the identity of the organizer, and nothing in these notes supplies any further event information.", "output": "Draft a standalone correction for the Northbank Record about the community supper described in the May 8 item “A supper at St. Luke’s.” Keep it to around 130–170 words, use plain, calm newspaper language, and make the corrected practical details easy to scan. This is a correction, not a new event preview, advertisement, apology essay, or invitation in the organizer’s voice.

The May 8 item incorrectly named St. Luke’s Church as the venue, gave June 15 as the date, and said the meal would start at 6:00 p.m. State that the supper is organized by East Ward Table, an independent volunteer group, and is not a church program. Give the correct location as Riverside Fellowship Hall, 22 Alder Street, with the entrance on Juniper Lane. The correct date is June 14; doors open at 5:15 p.m. and the meal begins at 5:30 p.m. Make clear that these are separate times and do not suggest the schedule has changed since publication. The supper is free, open to the neighborhood, and requires no reservation; those details were already correct.

If it fits naturally, include this exact quote from an East Ward Table volunteer coordinator, identified by role only: “We want neighbors to have the right door and the right evening.” Keep it as the coordinator’s statement, not the newspaper’s. Do not assign fault or explain how the mistake happened, imply that the church arranged or endorsed the event, or add information not supplied here, such as a contact name or reservation method. The correction may appear as text in the print edition and on the newspaper’s website; do not publish photos. No photograph is supplied. Write the correction as the newspaper setting the record straight, without implying that it has already run or received approval.

A possible heading is “Correction: East Ward Table supper details.”"}]
